headline: Chromosome-level and draft genome assemblies for non-model animal taxa
label: Non Model Animal Genome Assemblies
summary: Assemblies and annotations now span oyster, tilapia, plover, dolphin and springtail, with two studies extending into selection and gene-family analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the generation and annotation of reference genome assemblies for non-model animal taxa, with most items pairing assembly metrics with gene annotation. The Pacific oyster Magallana gigas assembly is a PacBio HiFi build of 707 Mb with contig N50 of 7.9 Mb and BUSCO 99.9%. The Mozambique tilapia Oreochromis mossambicus assembly is chromosome-level at 1.09 Gb, built from PacBio HiFi and Omni-C data, with 27,544 protein-coding genes annotated. The white-faced plover reference spans 1.25 Gb across 31 chromosomes with BUSCO 97.3%. What is new is the reference resource itself for these taxa. The Gangetic dolphin draft (2.53 Gb, BUSCO 97.73%, 27,983 genes) additionally reports 66 positively selected genes and an LGM-era population decline. The Antarctic springtail Cryptopygus antarcticus draft (103.6 Mb, N50 3.4 Mb, 19,808 genes) includes a glycoside hydrolase gene analysis, extending beyond assembly into gene-family diversity.
